em.justification:
Encounter type: EncounterType.OUTPATIENT. Objective evidence: "Musculoskeletal: No pain with right knee extension or flexion. Mild pain with right knee abduction or external rotation." Assessment/Plan evidence: "2. Right knee sprain - Assessment consistent with sprain related to recent increase in activity. - Recommend rest and avoidance of spinning/strenuous activity for at least one week. - Gradual return to exercise, starting with walking. - Knee brace when resuming activity. - OTC NSAIDs as needed. - Home knee-strengthening program reviewed; nurse provided exercises. - ... follow up in 4–6 weeks or sooner if pain persists/worsens to reassess need for further treatment or imaging."
1. problem_complexity: Low. Justification: 1 acute, uncomplicated illness or injury: Right knee sprain.
Right knee sprain: A&P documents new sprain due to recent activity with conservative management (rest, brace, OTC NSAIDs, home exercises) and contingent imaging if not improved. No systemic symptoms, no cross-system evaluation, and no evidence of complication or diagnostic uncertainty. Meets AMA definition of an acute, uncomplicated injury, which sets overall problem complexity to Low.
2. data_complexity: Minimal. Justification: Minimal Data Elements Present. Tests & Documents: 1 elements present. One unique test ordered during this encounter: CBC Panel (lab). No other tests/documents reviewed or ordered. Medication order does not count toward T&D.
3. risk_of_complications: Moderate. Justification: Highest risk item: Prescription drug management. The Orders list includes a named prescription medication order: "Lisinopril | Tablet (ordered)." Per guidelines, initiating a prescription medication is Moderate risk regardless of indication. Additional items: Named OTC management for knee pain ("OTC NSAIDs as needed") and OTC device recommendation ("Knee brace when resuming activity") are Low risk. Minimal-risk actions include wellness counseling and CBC lab order. Final risk must equal the highest identified risk, which is Moderate due to prescription drug management.

modifiers.description: Significant, Separately Identifiable Evaluation and Management Service by the Same Physician or Other Qualified Health Care Professional on the Same Day of the Procedure or Other Service
modifiers.justification: Two distinct E/M services on same DOS (preventive 99387 and problem-oriented 99203) by same provider. Documentation shows significant, separately identifiable problem-oriented E/M beyond the routine preventive exam, including targeted MSK history/exam and management plan for an acute knee sprain. Per CPT and NCCI, append 25 to the problem-oriented E/M when reported with a preventive E/M on the same date.
